boundary: THE EXPONENT CRITERION: a Weyl group element has pure Phi_d characteristic polynomial exactly when d is coprime to every exponent; then k = rank/phi(d), and a nondegenerate symplectic geometry W(k-1,p) follows when k is even, p = Phi_d(1) is prime, and p does not divide det(L). Controlled on E8, where it predicts d = 2,3,4,5,8 and no 16 -- exactly the brute-search result. Censused over every root system: E8 is the UNIQUE one with a qutrit geometry of content, a second independent proof that W(3,3) is E8-native

side_conditions: k even (a symplectic form needs even dimension)
p prime, i.e. d a prime power
p does not divide det(L), or the form degenerates
criterion.statement: a d-regular element has eigenvalues zeta_d^(-m_i) over the exponents, so its char poly is pure Phi_d^k exactly when gcd(d, m_i) = 1 for every exponent m_i
criterion.then: k = rank/phi(d), geometry W(k-1,p) with p = Phi_d(1)

e8_control.why_16_fails: phi(16) = 8 divides the rank, but 16 divides no E8 degree, so no 16-regular element exists -- which is the empirical gap that forced the rank-32 tower to use a 4-cycle

not_done: the same census for non-root lattices, e.g. Leech
whether B8's odd-unimodular qubit tower differs from E8's

qutrit_uniqueness.conclusion: E8 is the unique root system whose Weyl group supplies a nondegenerate qutrit geometry with content -- a second proof of E8-nativity, by exponents rather than by rank

obstructions.E6: 3-coprime and even rank, but k = 3 is ODD, and 3 divides det
obstructions.E8: k = 4, even, det 1 -- W(3,3), two qutrits
obstructions.F4: k = 2, giving W(1,3): four points on a line, no incidence content
obstructions.G2: k = 1 is odd, and 3 divides det
obstructions.classical: the exponent 3 is present, so d=3 is not exponent-coprime

vogel_lead.counterexample: F4 has Vogel beta = 5, which is NOT an F4 degree
vogel_lead.observation: for E6, E7, E8 the Vogel parameters (|alpha|, beta, gamma) are all degrees and t = alpha+beta+gamma is the largest degree, the Coxeter number
vogel_lead.status: a suggestive partial pattern, NOT a theorem; its only role was to point at the degrees, and no result here depends on it
